blocks.zh: 玻璃科學基礎：物理、化學與機械強度
blocks.en: Glass Science Fundamentals: Physical, Chemical and Mechanical Strength

blocks.zh: 學習目標 (Learning Objectives)
blocks.en: Learning Objectives

blocks.zh: 理解硼矽玻璃（Borosilicate, Type I）與鈉鈣矽玻璃（Soda-lime silicate, Type III）的組成差異及其在注射劑包裝中的選用依據。
blocks.en: Understand the compositional differences between borosilicate glass (Type I) and soda-lime silicate glass (Type III), and the basis for selecting each for injectable packaging.

blocks.zh: 掌握熱膨脹係數（CTE）對玻璃熱衝擊耐受性的影響，並了解為何壁厚會進一步改變此關係。
blocks.en: Understand how the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) affects a glass's tolerance to thermal shock, and why wall thickness further changes this relationship.

blocks.zh: 能夠解釋玻璃退火（Annealing）製程的目的，以及退火不完全對殘留應力與容器破裂風險的影響。
blocks.en: Be able to explain the purpose of glass annealing, and how incomplete annealing affects residual stress and the risk of container breakage.

blocks.zh: 理解 Griffith 方程式所描述的「應力 + 缺陷必須同時存在」才會導致破裂的核心原理，並能連結至實際操作風險。
blocks.en: Understand the core principle of the Griffith equation, that breakage requires stress and a flaw to be present at the same time, and link it to real handling risks.

blocks.zh: 了解吸附水層（Adsorption Water Layer）在玻璃表面的保護與潤滑作用，以及除熱原（Depyrogenation）製程如何破壞此層並提高損傷風險；並掌握化學強化（Chemical Strengthening）的離子交換機制及其實務效益。
blocks.en: Understand the protective and lubricating role of the adsorption water layer on the glass surface, and how depyrogenation destroys this layer and increases the risk of damage; and understand the ion-exchange mechanism of chemical strengthening and its practical benefits.

blocks.zh: 8.0 Introduction to Glass Types | 玻璃類型概論
blocks.en: 8.0 Introduction to Glass Types

blocks.zh: 核心概念解析
blocks.en: Key Concepts Explained

blocks.zh: Type I vs. Type III 的關鍵差異
blocks.en: Key Differences Between Type I and Type III

blocks.zh: 硼矽玻璃（Borosilicate glass）即 Type I 玻璃，是注射劑（Parenteral）包裝的標準選擇。其化學惰性強、熱膨脹係數低，不易與藥液反應，也耐受高低溫衝擊。
blocks.en: Borosilicate glass is Type I glass and the standard choice for parenteral packaging. It is highly chemically inert, has a low coefficient of thermal expansion, is unlikely to react with the drug solution, and tolerates both high and low temperature shocks.

blocks.zh: 鈉鈣矽玻璃（Soda-lime silicate glass）即 Type III，化學穩定性較低，僅適用於非注射劑（Non-parenteral）包裝，如口服液劑容器。
blocks.en: Soda-lime silicate glass is Type III. It has lower chemical stability and is suitable only for non-parenteral packaging, such as containers for oral liquids.

blocks.zh: 對 CDMO 而言，Type I 不可降級使用 — 若在壓力下改用 Type III，不僅違反 USP/EP 規範，更直接危及注射劑安全性。
blocks.en: For a CDMO, Type I must never be downgraded. Switching to Type III under pressure not only violates USP/EP requirements but also directly endangers the safety of the injectable product.

blocks.zh: 生活類比
blocks.en: Real-Life Analogy

blocks.zh: Type I 硼矽玻璃就像耐熱實驗室燒杯（Pyrex），Type III 鈉鈣矽玻璃則像一般飲料玻璃瓶。兩者都是玻璃，但面對高溫、化學接觸或急速冷卻時，差距非常大。
blocks.en: Type I borosilicate glass is like a heat-resistant laboratory beaker (Pyrex), while Type III soda-lime silicate glass is like an ordinary drinking-glass bottle. Both are glass, but the difference is very large when facing high temperature, chemical contact or rapid cooling.

blocks.zh: Table 8.0-1🔍: Overview of Glasses Used in Pharmaceutical Primary Packaging | 藥用玻璃分類總覽
blocks.en: Table 8.0-1🔍: Overview of Glasses Used in Pharmaceutical Primary Packaging

blocks.zh: 表格解讀重點
blocks.en: Key Points for Reading the Table

blocks.zh: CTE 數值的含義
blocks.en: What the CTE Values Mean

blocks.zh: CTE（熱膨脹係數，Coefficient of Thermal Expansion）數值越低，代表玻璃在溫度變化時膨脹/收縮幅度越小，熱衝擊耐受性越高。
blocks.en: The lower the CTE (coefficient of thermal expansion), the less the glass expands and contracts with temperature changes, and the higher its thermal shock resistance.

blocks.zh: Borosilicate 3.3：CTE ~3.3，最穩定，適合嚴苛溫度環境
blocks.en: Borosilicate 3.3: CTE ~3.3, the most stable, suitable for demanding temperature environments

blocks.zh: Borosilicate 5.0：CTE ~5，藥用最常見的 tubular vial 材質
blocks.en: Borosilicate 5.0: CTE ~5, the most common material for pharmaceutical tubular vials

blocks.zh: Soda-lime silicate：CTE ~7–9，熱穩定性最差，只適合 Type III
blocks.en: Soda-lime silicate: CTE ~7–9, the poorest thermal stability, suitable only for Type III

blocks.zh: Quartz：CTE <1，極端穩定但成本極高，非一般藥用
blocks.en: Quartz: CTE <1, extremely stable but very costly, not used for general pharmaceutical packaging

blocks.zh: 實務提醒：退火點（Annealing Point）
blocks.en: Practical Reminder: Annealing Point

blocks.zh: 退火點是製造工廠控制冷卻速率的關鍵溫度參數。不同玻璃類型的退火點差距不大（525–575°C），但退火冷卻速率的精確控制攸關最終容器的殘留應力水準。
blocks.en: The annealing point is the key temperature parameter used by the manufacturer to control the cooling rate. The annealing points of the different glass types are not far apart (525–575°C), but precise control of the annealing cooling rate determines the level of residual stress in the finished container.

blocks.zh: Quartz 的退火點超過 1150°C，說明其製造難度與成本遠高於其他材質。
blocks.en: The annealing point of quartz exceeds 1150°C, which shows why it is far more difficult and costly to manufacture than the other materials.

blocks.zh: 類比：CTE 好比彈性係數
blocks.en: Analogy: CTE Is Like Elasticity

blocks.zh: CTE 越高的玻璃，就像彈性越差的橡皮筋：快速拉伸或壓縮時，更容易斷裂。硼矽玻璃是「彈性較好」的材質，但仍是脆性材料（Brittle material），只是它的「安全邊際」更寬。
blocks.en: Glass with a higher CTE is like a rubber band with poorer elasticity: it breaks more easily when stretched or compressed quickly. Borosilicate glass is the "more elastic" material, but it is still a brittle material; it simply has a wider "safety margin".

blocks.zh: 8.1 Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE) | 熱膨脹係數
blocks.en: 8.1 Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE)

blocks.zh: 概念解析與實務意義
blocks.en: Concept and Practical Significance

blocks.zh: CTE 與熱衝擊耐受力的直接對比
blocks.en: Direct Comparison of CTE and Thermal Shock Resistance

blocks.zh: 以 0.5 mm 壁厚為例（理論值，無缺陷狀態）：
blocks.en: Taking a 0.5 mm wall thickness as the example (theoretical values, flawless condition):

blocks.zh: Soda-lime silicate（Type III）：耐 ~110°C 溫差
blocks.en: Soda-lime silicate (Type III): withstands a temperature difference of ~110°C

blocks.zh: Borosilicate 5.0（Type I）：耐 ~220°C 溫差
blocks.en: Borosilicate 5.0 (Type I): withstands a temperature difference of ~220°C

blocks.zh: Borosilicate 3.3（Type I）：耐 ~340°C 溫差
blocks.en: Borosilicate 3.3 (Type I): withstands a temperature difference of ~340°C

blocks.zh: 這正是注射劑選用 Type I 的物理依據：凍乾（Lyophilization）、除熱原（Depyrogenation, 350°C）等製程中的溫差遠超 Type III 的安全範圍。
blocks.en: This is the physical basis for choosing Type I for injectables: the temperature differences in processes such as lyophilization and depyrogenation (350°C) far exceed the safe range of Type III.

blocks.zh: 壁厚的雙重效應（重要！）
blocks.en: The Dual Effect of Wall Thickness (Important!)

blocks.zh: 玻璃導熱性差（Poor thermal conductivity）是理解壁厚影響的關鍵：
blocks.en: Poor thermal conductivity of glass is the key to understanding the effect of wall thickness:

blocks.zh: 薄壁：內外溫差小 → 熱衝擊風險低，但機械強度較弱
blocks.en: Thin wall: small temperature difference between inside and outside, so low thermal shock risk, but weaker mechanical strength

blocks.zh: 厚壁：內外溫差大 → 熱衝擊風險高，但可承受更大機械負荷
blocks.en: Thick wall: large temperature difference between inside and outside, so high thermal shock risk, but able to bear greater mechanical loads

blocks.zh: 設計選型時需在「熱抗性」與「機械強度」之間權衡，這也是 vial 規格設計的核心考量。
blocks.en: Design and selection must balance "thermal resistance" against "mechanical strength", which is a core consideration in vial specification design.

blocks.zh: 理論 vs. 實際的差距
blocks.en: Theory vs. Reality

blocks.zh: 報告明確指出：上述數據僅適用於「完美無瑕」（Flawless）的玻璃。現實中，玻璃表面必然存在微細缺陷（Micro-flaws）。因此，表面缺陷的影響往往比 CTE 更能決定玻璃的實際熱衝擊破裂風險。
blocks.en: The report states clearly that the above data apply only to "flawless" glass. In reality, glass surfaces inevitably carry microscopic flaws (micro-flaws). The effect of surface flaws is therefore often a better determinant of the actual risk of thermal shock breakage than CTE.

blocks.zh: 換句話說：一支有嚴重刮痕的 Borosilicate 3.3 vial，可能比一支完好的 Borosilicate 5.0 vial 更脆弱。這個認知貫穿整份 TR87 的操作建議。
blocks.en: In other words, a badly scratched Borosilicate 3.3 vial may be more fragile than an intact Borosilicate 5.0 vial. This understanding runs through all of the handling recommendations in TR87.

blocks.zh: 8.2 Stress Inside the Glass | 玻璃內部應力
blocks.en: 8.2 Stress Inside the Glass

blocks.zh: 玻璃固化行為解析
blocks.en: How Glass Solidifies

blocks.zh: 玻璃沒有固定熔點
blocks.en: Glass Has No Fixed Melting Point

blocks.zh: 結晶固體（如冰、金屬）在固定的熔點（T<sub>m</sub>）瞬間轉換固液態；玻璃不同，其黏度（Viscosity）隨溫度連續變化，是一種「過冷液體（Supercooled liquid）」的凍結狀態。
blocks.en: A crystalline solid (such as ice or metal) changes between solid and liquid instantly at a fixed melting point (T<sub>m</sub>); glass is different. Its viscosity changes continuously with temperature, and it is a frozen state of a "supercooled liquid".

blocks.zh: 這個特性使玻璃的成型與退火成為「速率控制」而非「溫度開關」的製程。
blocks.en: This property makes glass forming and annealing a "rate-controlled" process rather than a "temperature-switch" process.

blocks.zh: 三個關鍵溫度點（從高到低）
blocks.en: Three Key Temperature Points (from High to Low)

blocks.zh: 退火點（Annealing Point）：殘留應力在「數分鐘」內消散。為退火製程上限溫度，硼矽玻璃約 550–575°C。
blocks.en: Annealing point: residual stress dissipates within "minutes". This is the upper temperature limit of the annealing process, about 550–575°C for borosilicate glass.

blocks.zh: 玻璃轉換溫度（Tg）：結構從液態行為轉換為固態行為的過渡區間中點，介於退火點與應變點之間。
blocks.en: Glass transition temperature (Tg): the midpoint of the transition range in which the structure changes from liquid-like to solid-like behavior, lying between the annealing point and the strain point.

blocks.zh: 應變點（Strain Point）：殘留應力在「數小時」內消散。為退火製程下限溫度，低於此點結構不再重排。
blocks.en: Strain point: residual stress dissipates within "hours". This is the lower temperature limit of the annealing process; below this point the structure no longer rearranges.

blocks.zh: 類比：退火製程如同「慢慢放鬆」
blocks.en: Analogy: Annealing Is Like "Relaxing Slowly"

blocks.zh: 想像一條被過度扭緊的橡皮筋：若快速鬆手，它會彈開（裂開）；若緩慢、有控制地釋放，它就能回到自然狀態而不斷裂。退火正是讓玻璃原子有足夠時間重新排列，釋放成型時累積的應力。
blocks.en: Imagine a rubber band twisted too tightly: if you let go quickly, it springs apart (cracks); if you release it slowly and under control, it returns to its natural state without breaking. Annealing is exactly what gives the glass atoms enough time to rearrange and release the stress accumulated during forming.

blocks.zh: 應力的物理定義
blocks.en: Physical Definition of Stress

blocks.zh: 兩種核心應力類型
blocks.en: Two Core Types of Stress

blocks.zh: 拉伸應力（Tensile stress）：力使材料被拉開，原子間距離被拉大。玻璃「永遠在拉伸應力點破裂」。
blocks.en: Tensile stress: a force that pulls the material apart and increases the distance between atoms. Glass "always breaks at points of tensile stress".

blocks.zh: 壓縮應力（Compressive stress）：力使材料被壓縮，原子間距離縮小。玻璃對壓縮應力有較高耐受性；這也是化學強化的核心原理。
blocks.en: Compressive stress: a force that compresses the material and decreases the distance between atoms. Glass tolerates compressive stress much better; this is also the core principle of chemical strengthening.

blocks.zh: 重要觀念：施加壓縮力的一側，在容器其他位置往往同時產生拉伸應力，而這些拉伸應力區才是真正的危險點。
blocks.en: Important concept: where compressive force is applied on one side, tensile stress is often generated at the same time elsewhere in the container, and it is these tensile stress zones that are the real danger points.

blocks.zh: 製造熱應力與退火機制
blocks.en: Thermal Stress in Manufacturing and the Annealing Mechanism

blocks.zh: Tubular Vial 成型應力的來源
blocks.en: Sources of Forming Stress in Tubular Vials

blocks.zh: 玻璃管成型時，底部與開口受熱（>1000°C），中段管身保持較低溫。局部加熱 → 原子振動加劇 → 快速冷卻 → 原子來不及重排 → 「凍結」在非理想位置 → 產生拉伸與壓縮應力。
blocks.en: When glass tubing is formed into vials, the bottom and the opening are heated (>1000°C) while the middle of the tube body stays cooler. Localized heating leads to more intense atomic vibration, then rapid cooling, so the atoms have no time to rearrange and are "frozen" in non-ideal positions, producing tensile and compressive stress.

blocks.zh: 退火爐（Annealing Lehr）的功能：將整支 vial 加熱至 T<sub>g</sub> + 20°C，讓原子有時間重新排列，再以精確控制的速率緩冷，使應力均勻消散。
blocks.en: Function of the annealing lehr: the whole vial is heated to T<sub>g</sub> + 20°C to give the atoms time to rearrange, and is then cooled slowly at a precisely controlled rate so that the stress dissipates evenly.

blocks.zh: 退火不完全的後果
blocks.en: Consequences of Incomplete Annealing

blocks.zh: 若退火製程控制不當（溫度不夠、冷卻太快、爐內溫度不均）：
blocks.en: If annealing is poorly controlled (temperature too low, cooling too fast, uneven temperature in the lehr):

blocks.zh: 殘留應力留存於 vial 瓶底或瓶口轉角處
blocks.en: Residual stress remains at the vial base or at the corners of the neck

blocks.zh: 在後續處理（灌裝、壓蓋、輸送）時遇到外部衝擊，更易在拉伸應力區域破裂
blocks.en: When an external impact occurs during later handling (filling, capping, conveying), the vial is more likely to break in the tensile stress zones

blocks.zh: 可用偏振光儀（Polariscope）量測殘留應力分布
blocks.en: The distribution of residual stress can be measured with a polariscope

blocks.zh: 這也說明為何 vendor qualification 應包含殘留應力檢測，而非僅依賴尺寸規格。
blocks.en: This also explains why vendor qualification should include residual stress testing, rather than relying only on dimensional specifications.

blocks.zh: 除熱原（Depyrogenation）的雙重影響
blocks.en: The Dual Impact of Depyrogenation

blocks.zh: 除熱原加熱至 ~350°C，低於玻璃 T<sub>g</sub>（~550°C），因此不會引入新的熱應力。但這個製程存在另一種風險：
blocks.en: Depyrogenation heats the glass to ~350°C, which is below the glass T<sub>g</sub> (~550°C), so it does not introduce new thermal stress. However, this process carries another type of risk:

blocks.zh: 洗瓶後殘留水分可能導致瓶底局部冷卻，與外部熱空氣形成溫差 → 熱衝擊微裂縫
blocks.en: Residual moisture after washing may cool the vial base locally, creating a temperature difference with the hot external air, which leads to thermal shock microcracks

blocks.zh: 高溫下玻璃表面保護性吸附水層蒸發 → 表面暴露，金屬導軌接觸易產生刮痕 → 機械強度下降
blocks.en: At high temperature the protective adsorbed water layer on the glass surface evaporates, exposing the surface, so contact with metal guide rails easily causes scratches and a loss of mechanical strength

blocks.zh: 詳見第 8.4 節的吸附層討論。
blocks.en: See the discussion of the adsorption layer in Section 8.4.

blocks.zh: 低溫環境下的破裂機制
blocks.en: Breakage Mechanisms in Low-Temperature Environments

blocks.zh: 凍乾破裂的真正原因
blocks.en: The Real Cause of Breakage in Lyophilization

blocks.zh: 凍乾（Lyophilization）時 vial 暴露在 -40 至 -80°C，長期儲存（Cryopreservation）甚至到 -196°C（液氮）。但破裂的主因並非熱衝擊，而是：
blocks.en: During lyophilization, vials are exposed to -40 to -80°C, and in long-term storage (cryopreservation) down to -196°C (liquid nitrogen). However, the main cause of breakage is not thermal shock but:

blocks.zh: 內容物膨脹的機械應力：溶液結冰體積增大，向外施加壓力
blocks.en: Mechanical stress from expansion of the contents: the solution expands in volume when it freezes and exerts outward pressure

blocks.zh: 既有表面缺陷：瓶底與藥液接觸區域的微裂縫在應力下擴展
blocks.en: Pre-existing surface flaws: microcracks in the area of the vial base in contact with the drug solution grow under stress

blocks.zh: 結論：降低 CTE（選更好的玻璃）有幫助，但減少表面缺陷才是降低凍乾破裂率的根本策略。
blocks.en: Conclusion: lowering the CTE (choosing a better glass) helps, but reducing surface flaws is the fundamental strategy for lowering the lyophilization breakage rate.

blocks.zh: CDMO 實務啟示
blocks.en: Practical Implications for a CDMO

blocks.zh: 凍乾破裂風險管理重點：
blocks.en: Key points for managing lyophilization breakage risk:

blocks.zh: 進廠檢驗包含瓶底外觀及缺陷目視/自動檢查
blocks.en: Incoming inspection includes visual or automated inspection of the vial base for appearance and defects

blocks.zh: 選用缺陷率較低的 vendor（表面品質要求應列入規格書）
blocks.en: Select vendors with lower defect rates (surface quality requirements should be included in the specification)

blocks.zh: 灌裝後至進凍乾機前的輸送過程，最小化 vial 碰撞與刮傷
blocks.en: Minimize vial collisions and scratching during conveying from filling to the lyophilizer

blocks.zh: 凍乾配方開發時考慮結冰膨脹率，調整充填量
blocks.en: When developing the lyophilization formulation, consider the freezing expansion ratio and adjust the fill volume accordingly

blocks.zh: 8.3 Mechanical Strength of Glass | 玻璃機械強度
blocks.en: 8.3 Mechanical Strength of Glass

blocks.zh: 延性 vs. 脆性材料
blocks.en: Ductile vs. Brittle Materials

blocks.zh: 玻璃是脆性材料（Brittle material）
blocks.en: Glass Is a Brittle Material

blocks.zh: 金屬等延性材料（Ductile material）在斷裂前會先塑性變形（Plastic deformation）：可以彎曲、拉伸，給操作者「警告訊號」。
blocks.en: Ductile materials such as metals undergo plastic deformation before fracture: they can bend and stretch, giving the operator a "warning sign".

blocks.zh: 玻璃是脆性材料：原子來不及移動，就已在缺陷尖端被撕開。這意味著：
blocks.en: Glass is a brittle material: the atoms have no time to move before the material is torn apart at the tip of a flaw. This means:

blocks.zh: 破裂是突發性的，無預兆
blocks.en: Breakage is sudden and gives no warning

blocks.zh: 任何缺陷都是潛在的破裂起點
blocks.en: Any flaw is a potential origin of breakage

blocks.zh: 強調「預防」勝於「偵測」
blocks.en: The emphasis is on prevention rather than detection

blocks.zh: 類比：鉛筆 vs. 橡皮筋
blocks.en: Analogy: Pencil vs. Rubber Band

blocks.zh: 橡皮筋（延性）：拉到一半會變細、警告你快斷了。鉛筆（脆性）：用力一折，毫無預警地「啪」一聲斷掉。玻璃更像鉛筆，而且斷裂後碎片可能汙染無菌藥液。
blocks.en: A rubber band (ductile) thins out partway through stretching, warning you it is about to break. A pencil (brittle) snaps with a sudden "crack" when bent hard, with no warning. Glass is more like the pencil, and after breakage the fragments may contaminate the sterile drug solution.

blocks.zh: Griffith 方程式的實務意義
blocks.en: Practical Significance of the Griffith Equation

blocks.zh: 方程式解讀：三個可干預的變數
blocks.en: Interpreting the Equation: Three Variables You Can Act On

blocks.zh: σ（應力）：可透過製程設計降低。例如：優化輸送線速度、避免 vial 積壓、控制壓蓋力、使用彈性導軌。
blocks.en: σ (stress): can be reduced through process design, for example by optimizing conveyor line speed, avoiding vial back-up, controlling capping force, and using flexible guide rails.

blocks.zh: Y（幾何因子）：缺陷位置影響應力集中程度。瓶底角落（Corner flaw）比側面表面缺陷（Surface flaw）更危險，因為邊角的幾何放大效應更強。
blocks.en: Y (geometry factor): the position of the flaw affects the degree of stress concentration. A corner flaw at the vial base is more dangerous than a surface flaw on the side wall, because the geometric amplification effect at corners is stronger.

blocks.zh: c（缺陷深度）：深度缺陷（Deep flaw）遠比淺層刮痕危險。這是為什麼碰撞痕（Chipping）比細線刮痕（Scratch）對強度的影響更大。
blocks.en: c (flaw depth): a deep flaw is far more dangerous than a shallow scratch. This is why chipping affects strength more than a fine-line scratch does.

blocks.zh: 核心洞見：應力 + 缺陷必須同時存在
blocks.en: Core Insight: Stress and a Flaw Must Be Present Together

blocks.zh: 這是 TR87 Section 8 最重要的結論之一：
blocks.en: This is one of the most important conclusions of TR87 Section 8:

blocks.zh: 實務含義：
blocks.en: Practical implications:

blocks.zh: 沒有缺陷的玻璃，即使施加相當應力也不會輕易破裂
blocks.en: Glass without flaws will not easily break even under considerable stress

blocks.zh: 有缺陷但零應力，也不會破裂
blocks.en: Glass with flaws but zero stress will not break either

blocks.zh: 兩者同時存在 → 風險急遽上升
blocks.en: When both are present, the risk rises sharply

blocks.zh: 因此，風險控制策略需同時攻防兩個方向：減少缺陷（表面品質管理）+ 降低應力（製程與設備設計）。
blocks.en: Risk control strategy therefore needs to address both sides: reduce flaws (surface quality management) + reduce stress (process and equipment design).

blocks.zh: 常見應力來源對應 TR87 操作建議
blocks.en: Common Stress Sources and the Corresponding TR87 Handling Recommendations

blocks.zh: 垂直力（壓蓋）：在瓶頸外表面和瓶跟（Heel）產生拉伸應力 → 需控制壓蓋機扭矩/力道
blocks.en: Vertical force (capping): produces tensile stress on the outer surface of the neck and at the heel, so the capper torque/force must be controlled

blocks.zh: 側向擠壓（螺旋推進器、輸送積壓）：在受力點對側的外表面產生拉伸應力 → 需防止 vial 在輸送線上卡住
blocks.en: Lateral squeezing (screw feeders, conveyor back-up): produces tensile stress on the outer surface opposite the point of force, so vials must be prevented from jamming on the conveyor line

blocks.zh: 內部壓力（凍乾）：從容器內部向外施加應力 → 結冰膨脹是最主要來源
blocks.en: Internal pressure (lyophilization): stress applied outward from inside the container; freezing expansion is the main source

blocks.zh: 應力分布的實際模式
blocks.en: Actual Patterns of Stress Distribution

blocks.zh: 玻璃永遠在拉伸應力點破裂
blocks.en: Glass Always Breaks at Points of Tensile Stress

blocks.zh: 這個原則是操作風險評估的基礎。施力方向不等於破裂方向：
blocks.en: This principle is the basis for operational risk assessment. The direction of the applied force is not the direction of breakage:

blocks.zh: 壓蓋機（向下力）：壓縮力作用於側壁，但在瓶頸（Neck）外表面和瓶跟（Heel）產生拉伸應力 → 破裂常見於瓶頸或瓶底轉角
blocks.en: Capper (downward force): compressive force acts on the side wall, but tensile stress arises on the outer surface of the neck and at the heel, so breakage is common at the neck or the base corner

blocks.zh: 輸送線擠壓（側向力）：受力點的容器內表面及受力方向垂直 90° 的外表面產生拉伸應力 → 破裂可能發生在遠離接觸點的位置
blocks.en: Conveyor squeezing (lateral force): tensile stress arises on the inner surface of the container at the point of force and on the outer surface 90° perpendicular to the direction of force, so breakage can occur far from the contact point

blocks.zh: 這解釋了為何生產線上的破裂位置，有時看起來與施力方向「不合邏輯」。
blocks.en: This explains why the location of breakage on a production line sometimes looks "illogical" relative to the direction of the applied force.

blocks.zh: 表面狀態與強度的動態關係
blocks.en: The Dynamic Relationship Between Surface Condition and Strength

blocks.zh: 容器生命週期中的累積損傷
blocks.en: Cumulative Damage over the Container Life Cycle

blocks.zh: 每個接觸 vial 的步驟都可能累積損傷：製造 → 包裝 → 倉儲 → 進料 → 洗瓶 → 除熱原 → 灌裝 → 壓蓋 → 出料 → 目視檢查。
blocks.en: Every step that touches the vial may accumulate damage: manufacturing → packaging → warehousing → incoming feed → washing → depyrogenation → filling → capping → outfeed → visual inspection.

blocks.zh: 單一輕微損傷可能不足以造成破裂，但「累積效應」（Cumulative damage）加上製程應力就可能超過強度閾值。這是 TR87 強調全程監控（End-to-end monitoring）的原因。
blocks.en: A single minor injury may not be enough to cause breakage, but cumulative damage combined with process stress may exceed the strength threshold. This is why TR87 emphasizes end-to-end monitoring.

blocks.zh: 量測方法
blocks.en: Measurement Methods

blocks.zh: 破裂力（Break force）、強度（Strength）、及失效機率（Failure probability）量測可用於：
blocks.en: Measurement of break force, strength and failure probability can be used to:

blocks.zh: 比較不同 handling 步驟對強度的相對影響
blocks.en: Compare the relative effect of different handling steps on strength

blocks.zh: 評估新製程或新設備對 vial 完整性的衝擊
blocks.en: Evaluate the impact of a new process or new equipment on vial integrity

blocks.zh: 建立各製程步驟的「損傷基準線（Damage baseline）」
blocks.en: Establish a "damage baseline" for each process step

blocks.zh: 8.4 Adsorption Layer on the Glass | 玻璃表面吸附層
blocks.en: 8.4 Adsorption Layer on the Glass

blocks.zh: 吸附水層的保護與潤滑機制
blocks.en: Protective and Lubricating Mechanism of the Adsorbed Water Layer

blocks.zh: 吸附層的三個階段
blocks.en: Three Stages of the Adsorption Layer

blocks.zh: 第一階段（初始）：清潔或加熱後的玻璃表面迅速從空氣中吸附水分子，形成單分子層（Monolayer）
blocks.en: Stage 1 (initial): after cleaning or heating, the glass surface quickly adsorbs water molecules from the air, forming a monolayer

blocks.zh: 第二階段（數週後）：水分子逐漸擴散滲入表面更深層，形成更厚的保護層，防護能力增強
blocks.en: Stage 2 (after several weeks): water molecules gradually diffuse deeper into the surface, forming a thicker protective layer with stronger protection

blocks.zh: 第三階段（加熱後）：除熱原或高溫處理使保護層蒸發，表面重新「裸露」，且重建速度非常慢
blocks.en: Stage 3 (after heating): depyrogenation or high-temperature treatment evaporates the protective layer, leaving the surface "bare" again, and the layer rebuilds very slowly

blocks.zh: 關鍵洞見：刮傷是 Handling 問題，不是材質問題
blocks.en: Key Insight: Scratching Is a Handling Problem, Not a Material Problem

blocks.zh: TR87 明確指出：「Scratches and sticking behavior is a matter of glass handling rather than the composition of glass itself.」
blocks.en: TR87 states clearly: "Scratches and sticking behavior is a matter of glass handling rather than the composition of glass itself."

blocks.zh: 除熱原後 vial 剛出爐時，表面保護層已蒸發 → 這是整個製程中玻璃最脆弱的時刻
blocks.en: When vials come out of depyrogenation, the surface protective layer has evaporated, so this is the most fragile moment for the glass in the whole process

blocks.zh: 此時進行高速輸送或與金屬表面接觸，刮傷風險最高
blocks.en: High-speed conveying or contact with metal surfaces at this point carries the highest scratch risk

blocks.zh: 浸水無法加速保護層重建（反應動力學（Kinetics）太慢）
blocks.en: Soaking in water cannot speed up rebuilding of the protective layer (the reaction kinetics are too slow)

blocks.zh: 兩種不同成分的玻璃，若 handling 方式一致，刮傷傾向相近
blocks.en: Two glasses of different composition tend to scratch to a similar degree if handled in the same way

blocks.zh: 類比：防曬乳的比喻
blocks.en: Analogy: Sunscreen

blocks.zh: 吸附水層就像皮膚上的天然油脂層：洗澡（清潔 = 除熱原）之後，皮膚最乾燥、最脆弱。需要一段時間才能重新分泌足夠的保護油脂。玻璃的吸附層機制與此非常相似。
blocks.en: The adsorbed water layer is like the natural oil layer on skin: right after a bath (cleaning = depyrogenation), the skin is at its driest and most fragile, and it takes time to secrete enough protective oil again. The adsorption layer mechanism of glass is very similar.

blocks.zh: 灌裝線速度優化的科學依據
blocks.en: Scientific Basis for Optimizing Filling Line Speed

blocks.zh: 吸附水層也是 lubricant（潤滑劑），降低 vial 與 vial 之間、vial 與金屬導軌之間的摩擦係數（COF）。
blocks.en: The adsorbed water layer is also a lubricant, lowering the coefficient of friction (COF) between vials and between vials and metal guide rails.

blocks.zh: 在吸附層完整的條件下，可適度提高灌裝線速度而不顯著增加刮傷率。但除熱原後剛進入灌裝線的 vial，應特別注意輸送速度控制，或使用外部潤滑措施（如 Section 8.5 的化學強化塗層）。
blocks.en: Where the adsorption layer is intact, filling line speed can be raised moderately without significantly increasing the scratch rate. However, for vials that have just entered the filling line after depyrogenation, conveying speed should be controlled with particular care, or external lubrication measures should be used (such as the chemical strengthening coating in Section 8.5).

blocks.zh: 8.5 Chemical Strengthening | 化學強化
blocks.en: 8.5 Chemical Strengthening

blocks.zh: 離子交換強化機制解析
blocks.en: The Ion-Exchange Strengthening Mechanism

blocks.zh: 化學強化的核心原理
blocks.en: Core Principle of Chemical Strengthening

blocks.zh: 離子交換（Ion exchange）製程將玻璃表面層的小離子換成大離子，迫使表面受到壓縮應力（Compressive stress）：
blocks.en: The ion exchange process replaces small ions in the glass surface layer with larger ions, forcing the surface into compressive stress:

blocks.zh: Na⁺（較小）→ K⁺（較大，半徑差約 0.38 Å）
blocks.en: Na⁺ (smaller) → K⁺ (larger, radius difference about 0.38 Å)

blocks.zh: K⁺ 嵌入後「撐開」周圍空間 → 表面持續受到壓縮力
blocks.en: Once embedded, K⁺ "wedges apart" the surrounding space, so the surface remains under continuous compression

blocks.zh: 要讓裂縫擴展，外部拉伸應力必須先克服這層壓縮預力 → 大幅提高破裂閾值
blocks.en: For a crack to propagate, the external tensile stress must first overcome this compressive pre-load, which greatly raises the breakage threshold

blocks.zh: 這與鋼化玻璃（Tempered glass）的原理類似，但化學方法可處理複雜形狀（如 vial）而不需要快速風冷。
blocks.en: The principle is similar to tempered glass, but the chemical method can treat complex shapes (such as vials) without the need for rapid air cooling.

blocks.zh: 化學強化的多重效益
blocks.en: Multiple Benefits of Chemical Strengthening

blocks.zh: 防止裂縫擴展（Crack propagation）：表面壓縮層物理性封閉裂縫路徑
blocks.en: Prevents crack propagation: the surface compressive layer physically closes off the crack path

blocks.zh: 抑制玻璃微粒生成（Particulate generation）：減少碎裂風險，對注射劑安全性有直接意義
blocks.en: Suppresses particulate generation: reduces the risk of fragmentation, with direct significance for injectable safety

blocks.zh: 提升整體機械強度：高應力負載（如壓蓋）下的破裂機率下降
blocks.en: Raises overall mechanical strength: lowers the probability of breakage under high stress loads (such as capping)

blocks.zh: 適用所有玻璃類型：前提是含有足夠的 Na⁺（鋁矽玻璃、硼矽玻璃、鈉鈣矽玻璃均可）
blocks.en: Applicable to all glass types: provided they contain enough Na⁺ (aluminosilicate, borosilicate and soda-lime silicate glass can all be used)

blocks.zh: 製程限制：必須在最終容器上處理
blocks.en: Process Limitation: Must Be Done on the Final Container

blocks.zh: 由於玻璃管在成型（Forming）過程中會受熱，化學強化產生的壓縮層會被破壞。因此，化學強化製程必須在容器成型完成後才能進行，不能在玻璃管階段預先處理。
blocks.en: Because glass tubing is heated during forming, the compressive layer produced by chemical strengthening would be destroyed. Chemical strengthening must therefore be carried out after container forming is complete and cannot be applied to the glass tubing beforehand.

blocks.zh: 這也意味著：化學強化是下游（Downstream）工序，需整合到容器供應鏈中，而非原材料規格問題。
blocks.en: This also means that chemical strengthening is a downstream operation that must be integrated into the container supply chain, and is not a raw material specification issue.

blocks.zh: 類比：預壓混凝土
blocks.en: Analogy: Pre-Stressed Concrete

blocks.zh: 化學強化就像預力混凝土（Pre-stressed concrete）：在鋼筋上先施加預壓力，讓混凝土在受外部拉力前必須先克服這個預壓。化學強化的壓縮層就是玻璃表面的「預壓鋼筋」。
blocks.en: Chemical strengthening is like pre-stressed concrete: a pre-load is first applied to the steel reinforcement so that the concrete must overcome this pre-load before it is subjected to external tension. The compressive layer from chemical strengthening is the "pre-stressed reinforcement" of the glass surface.

blocks.zh: 保護塗層（Protective Coating）的附加效益
blocks.en: Added Benefit of a Protective Coating

blocks.zh: 在化學強化的基礎上，外表面施加保護性塗層（如 SiO₂ 或有機薄膜）可進一步降低摩擦係數（COF），減少灌裝線上的滑動接觸損傷。這兩種措施是相輔相成的，可組合使用於高風險/高價值產品。
blocks.en: On top of chemical strengthening, applying a protective coating (such as SiO₂ or an organic thin film) to the outer surface can further lower the coefficient of friction (COF) and reduce sliding-contact damage on the filling line. The two measures complement each other and can be combined for high-risk or high-value products.

blocks.zh: 8.6 References for Appendix I | 參考文獻
blocks.en: 8.6 References for Appendix I

blocks.zh: 文獻重要性說明
blocks.en: Why the References Matter

blocks.zh: 標準規範文件
blocks.en: Standards and Specification Documents

blocks.zh: ASTM E228 / ISO 7991：CTE 量測方法的標準依據，用於供應商規格確認
blocks.en: ASTM E228 / ISO 7991: standard basis for CTE measurement methods, used to confirm supplier specifications

blocks.zh: ISO 12775 / ASTM E438：硼矽玻璃成分規格標準，是 Type I 玻璃原材料驗收的參照基準
blocks.en: ISO 12775 / ASTM E438: standards for borosilicate glass composition, the reference basis for incoming acceptance of Type I glass raw material

blocks.zh: USP <660> / Ph. Eur. 3.2.1：藥用玻璃容器法規分類標準，直接決定 Type I/II/III 的合規要求
blocks.en: USP <660> / Ph. Eur. 3.2.1: regulatory classification standards for pharmaceutical glass containers, which directly determine the compliance requirements for Type I/II/III

blocks.zh: Griffith 理論的歷史地位
blocks.en: Historical Standing of the Griffith Theory

blocks.zh: Griffith 1921 年的原始論文距今已逾百年，卻仍是現代破裂力學（Fracture Mechanics）的奠基之作。TR87 引用此理論，代表 K = σ × Y × √c 方程式在玻璃工業中的應用已經過充分驗證，可作為風險評估的量化工具。
blocks.en: Griffith's original 1921 paper is more than a hundred years old, yet it remains the foundation of modern fracture mechanics. TR87's citation of this theory shows that the application of the equation K = σ × Y × √c in the glass industry has been thoroughly validated and can serve as a quantitative tool for risk assessment.

blocks.zh: Section 8.0 Summary | 本節重點總結（繁體中文）
blocks.en: Section 8.0 Summary

blocks.zh: 玻璃類型選擇的物理依據：Type I 硼矽玻璃（Borosilicate）的低 CTE（3.3–5.0 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹）使其熱衝擊耐受力遠超 Type III 鈉鈣矽玻璃（7.1–9.3 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹），這是注射劑必須使用 Type I 的物理基礎，而非單純的法規要求。
blocks.en: Physical basis for glass type selection: the low CTE of Type I borosilicate glass (3.3–5.0 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹) gives it far greater thermal shock resistance than Type III soda-lime silicate glass (7.1–9.3 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹). This is the physical basis for why Type I must be used for injectables, not merely a regulatory requirement.

blocks.zh: 退火完整性決定殘留應力水準：玻璃成型後必須在退火爐（Annealing Lehr）中以精確速率冷卻，使應力在退火點至應變點範圍內充分消散。退火不完全的 vial，在後續製程的外部應力下更易在拉伸應力集中區域破裂。
blocks.en: Annealing integrity determines the level of residual stress: after forming, glass must be cooled in an annealing lehr at a precise rate so that stress dissipates fully between the annealing point and the strain point. Vials that are incompletely annealed are more likely to break in tensile stress concentration zones under external stress in later processes.

blocks.zh: 破裂的雙重條件：根據 Griffith 方程式 K = σ × Y × √c，破裂只有在「足夠應力」與「既有缺陷」同時存在且超過玻璃斷裂韌性時才會發生。這意味著風險控制必須雙管齊下：減少表面缺陷（精細 handling）+ 降低操作應力（設備與製程設計）。
blocks.en: Two conditions for breakage: according to the Griffith equation K = σ × Y × √c, breakage occurs only when "sufficient stress" and a "pre-existing flaw" are present together and exceed the fracture toughness of the glass. Risk control must therefore work on both fronts: reduce surface flaws (careful handling) + reduce handling stress (equipment and process design).

blocks.zh: 吸附水層保護機制：玻璃表面的吸附水層（Adsorption water layer）兼具保護與潤滑功能。除熱原（350°C）後此層蒸發，且無法透過水浸快速重建。因此，剛完成除熱原的 vial 是整個製程中最易受刮傷的時間點，需特別控制輸送速度與接觸條件。
blocks.en: Protection by the adsorbed water layer: the adsorbed water layer on the glass surface provides both protection and lubrication. After depyrogenation (350°C) this layer evaporates and cannot be quickly rebuilt by soaking in water. Vials that have just completed depyrogenation are therefore the most scratch-prone point in the whole process, and conveying speed and contact conditions need special control.

blocks.zh: 化學強化是現代損傷防護技術：以 KNO₃ 熔浴進行離子交換（Na⁺ → K⁺），在 vial 表面建立壓縮應力層，需在最終容器上進行（不能預先處理玻璃管）。化學強化能抑制裂縫擴展、減少玻璃微粒生成，並提升對高應力負載的整體耐受性，是高價值注射劑產品的重要風險緩解措施。
blocks.en: Chemical strengthening is a modern damage-protection technology: ion exchange in a molten KNO₃ bath (Na⁺ → K⁺) builds a compressive stress layer on the vial surface and must be done on the final container (not on glass tubing beforehand). Chemical strengthening suppresses crack propagation, reduces particulate generation and raises overall tolerance of high stress loads, making it an important risk mitigation measure for high-value injectable products.
